title: Tuning Andreev reflection and conductance in proximitized nanowires through the spin-orbit field direction
abstract: We investigate the Andreev reflection (AR) and the nonlinear conductance in a normal-superconductor junction realized with a proximitized semiconductor nanowire exposed to a magnetic field along its axis. We show that, while at zero energy the AR coefficient is determined by the topological phase of the superconducting side of the junction, at finite energy the AR is strongly affected by the directions of the Rashba spin-orbit field characterizing the normal and the proximitized sides. The tunability of the AR and the nonlinear conductance as a function of the spin-orbit misalignment angle is particularly pronounced when the proximitized side is in the topologically trivial phase. The spin-orbit field direction is revealed to be an efficient knob to control the electron transport through the hybrid junction, realizing an electrically widely tunable device. The implementation in realistic setups is discussed.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes Andreev reflection and conductance in semiconductor nanowires coupled to a superconductor. By controlling the relative direction of the spin-orbit field across the junction, the authors demonstrate a strong, electrically tunable control mechanism over electron transport. This suggests a pathway for realizing highly controllable superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the spin-orbit field direction can be used to tune Andreev reflection (AR) and nonlinear conductance in a hybrid normal-superconductor nanowire junction.
main_result: The AR and conductance are strongly tunable by misaligning the spin-orbit field between the normal and superconducting sides, offering an electrically controllable device.
method: The analysis employs the Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) equations and the scattering matrix method to calculate transport properties.
model_or_system: The system is a normal-superconductor (N-S) junction realized in a proximitized semiconductor nanowire exposed to a magnetic field. The physics is modeled using a four-component Nambu spinor field governed by the BdG Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Andreev reflection (AR) coefficient ($\mathcal{R}_e$) and nonlinear conductance ($G$).
important_parameters: The SO field misalignment angle ($\phi_{SO}$), the applied magnetic field ($b$), and the energy level ($E$).
main_assumptions: The SO field inhomogeneity is assumed to arise from differences in material deposition or screening between the N-side and S-side, and the model assumes a single-channel nanowire.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the physical setup, showing the N-S junction geometry and the relative orientation of the SO field vectors ($\alpha_N, \alpha_S$) and the magnetic field $b$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian in the BdG form, solves the resulting differential equations using the scattering matrix formalism, and analyzes the resulting transport coefficients based on the relative SO field angle.
why_interesting: The ability to use spin-orbit coupling direction as an electrical knob to control superconducting proximity effects and transport is highly relevant for building tunable quantum devices.
